agents.name: Codex

surface_source.quote: Runs Claude Code or Codex CLI in parallel worktrees, sandboxed away from your personal files and credentials.

agents.quote: My daily driver of choice is OpenAI Codex but I run out of tokens more quickly so have learned to be fine with either.

history.quote: I've been using AI tools since early 2021 when I was invited to test out the Copilot internal alpha at GitHub (where I spent 10 years).

agents.name: Claude Code

surface_source.quote: Once installed (`brew install sandvault`), you can run `sv codex` or `sv claude` to start your agent of choice or `sv shell` to start a shell.

agents.quote: By the end of a weekend with Claude Max and Anthropic's Fable 5 model and ~4 hours interacting with my computer I had something that sort of worked.

agents.quote:

models.name: Fable 5
models.quote: By the end of a weekend with Claude Max and Anthropic's Fable 5 model and ~4 hours interacting with my computer I had something that sort of worked.

history.quote: Claude Code (Opus 4.6 `max`): fairly stupid by default, can be nudged with aggressive hooks/tools/prompts to being less so

models.name: OpenAI Codex 5.4
models.quote: OpenAI Codex (5.4 `xhigh`): takes a while, generally does things mostly right first time, doesn't need much prompting/steering

review_style.value: Reviews agent work before pushing it himself; depth depends on the code
review_style.quote: I always review any agent-produced work as my normal user in the same shared worktree before I share it with others.

also.quote: How many of these I do depends on my familiarity with the code, its criticality and how confident I am in other guardrails e.g. CI, human review.
The wildest part: I have not (deliberately) read a single line of Swift code.
open a PR, wait for CI results and code review from humans or Copilot

harness.value: AgentIDE (his own Mac app) on sandvault, herdr and git worktrees
harness.quote: I'm now completely off Superset and almost entirely off Fork and Zed by (vibe) building my own tool: [AgentIDE](https://github.com/MikeMcQuaid/AgentIDE/).

history.value: Superset worktrees running agents under sandvault, Fork and Zed for review
history.quote: Superset creates the worktree under `/Users/Shared/sv-mike/worktrees` and launches the agent as the Sandvault user inside it.

rules_files.value: AGENTS-GLOBAL.md (19 lines), shared by Claude and Codex, kept minimal
rules_files.quote: Before finishing, check your work, identify what the user may not have considered in relation to their goals and ask useful follow-up questions, including what they should have asked.

value: git pre-push hook rejecting AI attribution trailers
hooks.quote: reject "has AI attribution; remove it and disclose AI use in the PR description."

signature.caption: his own vibe-built agent IDE
signature.why: Our pick: he replaced Superset, Fork and Zed with a native app he built for sandboxed agents in parallel worktrees, now in Homebrew.
signature.quote: It's an "agentic IDE" built by me just for my workflows and it has made me more productive and happy working with agents.

archetype.why: Built his own agent IDE on sandvault and worktrees instead of adapting someone else's.

signature_quote.value: The combination of sandboxing and worktrees means I can just throw more tokens at more problems and get more done.
